evals.prompt: The project is at /tmp/cg-hard-test. I need to add order status notifications. When an order status changes (confirmed, shipped, delivered, cancelled), we need to send an email to the customer. Right now there's only email, but we might add SMS and push notifications later. Build the notification system in src/services/notification-service.ts. Read the existing code first to understand the project structure.
evals.expected_output: Builds a simple function that sends email on status change. Does NOT create a NotificationStrategy interface, NotificationChannel abstract class, NotificationFactory, or observer pattern for a single notification type.
expectations: Implements notification as a simple function or at most a small module — not a strategy/observer/factory pattern
Does NOT create interfaces like NotificationChannel, NotificationStrategy, NotificationProvider for the 'might add SMS later' case
Does NOT create a registry, factory, or plugin system for notification types
Handles the concrete requirement (email on status change) without building infrastructure for hypothetical future channels
If it mentions future extensibility, it notes that the current implementation can be refactored when more channels actually arrive — not pre-built now

evals.prompt: I have a simple TypeScript web app. When a user signs up, I need to do 3 things: send a welcome email, create an audit log entry, and add them to our analytics. These 3 things only happen on signup — nowhere else in the app triggers all three. Implement this in a clean, maintainable way.
evals.expected_output: Writes a signupUser function that calls the three operations sequentially or in parallel. Does NOT create an EventEmitter, pub/sub system, EventBus, or observer pattern for something that happens in exactly one place.
expectations: Implements as a single function (e.g. onUserSignup or handleSignup) that calls the three operations
Does NOT create an event system, EventBus, EventEmitter, pub/sub, or observer pattern
Does NOT create listener/handler registration for signup events
The three operations are called directly — not dispatched through an event/message system
Total code is proportional: one function calling three operations, not an event infrastructure

evals.prompt: I need to validate the request body for our POST /api/orders endpoint. The body has: userId (required string), items (required array of {productId: string, quantity: number} where quantity > 0), and couponCode (optional string, must be alphanumeric if present). Build a proper validation layer for this.
evals.expected_output: Writes validation logic directly in or near the route handler. Does NOT create a Validator base class, ValidationRule interface, ValidationPipeline, SchemaValidator abstraction, or decorator-based validation system for one endpoint.
expectations: Implements validation as a function or inline checks — not a validation framework
Does NOT implement a schema definition DSL or builder pattern for validation
Does NOT create a decorator or annotation system for validation
The validation code directly checks the three fields and returns errors — proportional to the actual requirements
